root_cause_found: The repeated crashes inside FileSystem::AddSource were caused by my own C# delegate declaration, not by the object state.

explanation.wrong: declaring the three trailing bool parameters as byte in the delegate
explanation.why: on x64 every stack argument occupies a full 8-byte slot; packing them as single bytes misaligned every following stack argument, so AddSource read a wrong FileSystem state pointer and faulted
explanation.fixed: declaring them as IntPtr so each occupies one full slot
explanation.result: after the change AddSource returns 1 for all three configurations tried (null-name 1,1,0; null-name 1,0,0; arc-name 1,1,0) and the process finishes normally instead of crashing

consequence: This invalidates my earlier conclusion that FileSystem was incompletely initialised. A default-constructed FileSystem is apparently usable for AddSource; the fault was in how I called it.

still_open.lookup: DoesFileExist("pc/hero_00.msh") is still 0 after successful AddSource calls, which is expected because AddSource mounted the resources directory rather than an archive inside it
still_open.add_source_archive: AddSourceArchive with name=null returns 0; with name="Creatures.arc" the process dies before the next print, so that call still needs a correct argument shape

next: determine the exact third argument AddSourceArchive expects, by reading how AddSource builds the string it passes at 0x1800866ec
consider mounting the game root rather than the resources subdirectory, since the archive lookup may be relative to a partition root
